intent: Unify HUG-DBOS desktop and client presentation with the Empyrean aiX visual system: coherent navy/ice themes, native theme ownership, SVG iconography, branded empty/start/error views and usable configuration layouts. Preserve Run controls, permissions, storage locations, existing navigation and user WIP. Verify the exact GUI and its contracts rather than EDA or model business effectiveness.

The three test modules import node:test and execute the returned module factory using createRequire; none supplies a document. scripts/run-contract-tests.mjs only preloads the SSH guard for local tests, not a DOM. This is source inspection; no test command was run by this reviewer.
findings.suggested_fix: Update the three served-bundle registration harnesses to evaluate the bundle with an isolated document implementing the DOM operations used by apply (or an existing real DOM environment), retain effect cleanup callbacks, and run their existing registration assertions. Assert style/class installation and cleanup, including the already-branded case; keep production apply's browser behavior intact.
findings.title: Adapt bundle contract tests to the new DOM effect
findings.why_it_matters: Existing served-bundle contract tests now throw ReferenceError before checking any slot registrations. view.test.ts, view-run.test.ts and window.test.ts evaluate the real client bundle in Node and immediately execute effect callbacks without a document, so the newly unconditional DOM effect breaks the required regression suite. Providing an isolated DOM to those harnesses also lets them verify that unloading removes the injected style and preserves a pre-existing branding class.
findings.validation_reason: When the served-bundle tests reach apply(), test/contract/view.test.ts:214-234, view-run.test.ts:451-464 and window.test.ts:99-112 evaluate the module in Node and immediately invoke effects without a document, so the DOM effect newly added at packages/harness/src/client/index.ts:148-160 throws ReferenceError before registration assertions; the build entry and callers establish reachability, while incidence was not measured by running the suite.

evidence: packages/desktop/src/main.ts:581 -- icon: path.join(packageDir, 'assets/icon.png'),

Trigger: build and install a supported macOS arm64 package using scripts/package-trial.mjs. Its lines 855 and 858 select Electron.app and execute cpSync(electronApp, app, { recursive: true, dereference: false, verbatimSymlinks: true }).

The actual installed Electron template at node_modules/.pnpm/electron@44.2.0/node_modules/electron/dist/Electron.app/Contents/Info.plist:9-10 contains <key>CFBundleIconFile</key> followed by <string>electron.icns</string>.

scripts/package-trial.mjs:914-922 rewrites executable, display name, identifier, name and versions, then writes the plist; it leaves CFBundleIconFile intact. The copied desktop package is staged under the app resource directory at lines 861-862, so its assets/icon.png does not replace Contents/Resources/electron.icns.

packages/desktop/scripts/make-icon.mjs:85-87 emits only assets/icon.png. Targeted searches of packages/desktop/src and scripts/package-trial.mjs find no dock.setIcon, ICNS generation/copy, or CFBundleIconFile override. The new startup page embeds the PNG at packages/desktop/src/main.ts:349, so the in-window and installed native identities visibly diverge.

docs/specs/aixui/spec.zh-CN.md:25 requires the desktop title, startup/error page and App icon to adopt the same brand; docs/product-definition.md lists macOS arm64 as a delivery target. This is the new branding's interaction with the existing packaging path, not a request to rename persistent identities.
findings.suggested_fix: Generate a macOS ICNS asset from the same aiX artwork, install it into the packaged app's Contents/Resources before signing, and set CFBundleIconFile to that asset in scripts/package-trial.mjs. Keep the existing executable, bundle identifier and storage identities. For development launches, set app.dock?.setIcon to the existing PNG after readiness if the Dock must also show the brand.
findings.title: Packaged macOS installs retain the Electron app icon
findings.why_it_matters: A macOS user installing the packaged aiX upgrade still sees the Electron icon in Finder and the app switcher, despite the new aiX icon inside the startup page. The new PNG reaches the BrowserWindow and HTML, but the macOS packaging path copies Electron.app unchanged and retains its CFBundleIconFile pointing to electron.icns. This misses the explicit requirement that the App icon use the new brand on a supported delivery platform.
findings.validation_reason: For a macOS arm64 package built by scripts/package-trial.mjs, the new aiX App-icon requirement at docs/specs/aixui/spec.zh-CN.md:26 remains unmet: packaging copies Electron 44.2.0's Electron.app at lines 854-858 and preserves its CFBundleIconFile=electron.icns at lines 914-922, while the changed artwork only replaces assets/icon.png and no packaging or desktop code installs a branded native icon; this newly exposes the existing packaging limitation through the aiX branding change, and installed-package incidence was not measured.
